title: Windows GPU unit tests job fails with PowerShell execution policy error before running tests
signature: windows gpu unit tests extract openvino packages setupvars.ps1 cannot be loaded because running scripts is disabled on this system pssecurityexception unauthorizedaccess|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step fails: a dot-sourced PowerShell script cannot be loaded because script execution is disabled on the runner.

root_cause: After a successful artifact download and archive expansion in the 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step, the workflow dot-sources a generated temp PowerShell script (likely wrapping setupvars.ps1 / env setup) via '. <tempfile>.ps1'. The self-hosted Windows runner's current PowerShell execution policy (Restricted, the Windows default) blocks running any unsigned/local scripts, so the dot-source throws PSSecurityException/UnauthorizedAccess and the step exits with code 1. This is a runner/host configuration issue (ExecutionPolicy), not a code defect in the PR that triggered this push - the same signature has now recurred 3 times across different commits, consistent with a persistent misconfiguration on one or more self-hosted Windows GPU runners (or a runner image regression that reset/removed the RemoteSigned policy).
reproduction_steps: Not directly reproducible locally unless using an equivalent self-hosted Windows runner image. To confirm: on the affected Windows runner, open PowerShell and run `Get-ExecutionPolicy -List`; if `LocalMachine`/`Process`/`CurrentUser` scope resolves to `Restricted` (not `RemoteSigned` or `Bypass`), any `. <script>.ps1` dot-source invocation will fail identically. Reproduce by running `powershell -command ". 'C:\path\to\any.ps1'"` with ExecutionPolicy set to Restricted.
recommended_actions: Set the PowerShell execution policy on the affected self-hosted Windows GPU runner(s) to RemoteSigned (or Bypass for CI-only scope), e.g. `Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope LocalMachine -Force`, and verify it persists across runner restarts/re-imaging.
Update the Windows runner provisioning/image script (if runners are re-imaged) to set the execution policy as part of baseline setup so it isn't reset on each fresh VM.

As a workflow-level mitigation, invoke the generated script via `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File <script>.ps1` or `pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command ". '<script>.ps1'"` instead of a bare dot-source, so the step is resilient to host-level policy regressions.
Audit which self-hosted Windows runner pool/labels hosted this run and the two prior occurrences to identify whether it's a single misconfigured host or a fleet-wide image issue.
prevention_strategies: Bake the ExecutionPolicy setting into the Windows runner golden image/provisioning scripts instead of relying on manual one-off fixes, and add a lightweight runner self-check (e.g., a startup health check job) that verifies `Get-ExecutionPolicy` before accepting GPU test jobs. Prefer invoking all generated PowerShell helper scripts with an explicit `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` flag in the workflow/action itself so CI is not dependent on host policy defaults.
historical_context: This exact signature (PSSecurityException/UnauthorizedAccess dot-sourcing a temp .ps1 during 'Extract OpenVINO packages' on the GPU unit tests job) was previously recorded twice: run 43906839059 (commit 739714d6de9660afe2be5670313cf8a55434da78) and run 43883526619 (commit a1f0ea08348c50d407601b0fa2e451162aa939fb), both on 2026-11-16. This is now the 3rd occurrence, confirming a persistent/recurring runner-level misconfiguration rather than a one-off fluke.
